summary: Assessment for transistor-level threats focusing on reliability and security against parameter manipulation and degradation.

threats.deployment_consequence: Difficult to detect and mitigate post-deployment without design-based protections.
threats.description: Unauthorized manipulation of operating parameters such as voltage to induce faults or degrade device performance.
threats.potential_impact: Device malfunction, reliability degradation, potential data corruption.
threats.priority_rationale: High potential impact in operational environments where exposure to electrical attack is possible.
threats.scenario: An attacker uses voltage glitching to induce faulty behaviors in NMOS devices.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Threats become significant as devices operate in uncontrolled environments.
threats.title: Parameter Manipulation

threats.deployment_consequence: Aging effects are irreversible and necessitate robust initial design to mitigate.
threats.description: Accelerated transistor aging due to environmental stressors, leading to reliability issues or unintended device behavior.
threats.priority_rationale: Moderate priority due to environmental control difficulty, but significant in longevity-critical applications.
threats.scenario: Exposure to high temperatures accelerates Bias-Temperature Instability (BTI) in PMOS.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Environmental factors affect transistor aging after deployment.
threats.title: Aging and Degradation Abuse

threats.deployment_consequence: Difficult to address without preemptive design measures.
threats.description: Susceptibility to deliberate fault injections that exploit transient hardware faults.
threats.priority_rationale: High urgency for secure environments like financial processing where transient faults can be exploited.
threats.scenario: Electromagnetic interference causes transient faults in FinFETs during operation.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Manifests through inadequate supply chain verification or insufficient fault-tolerant design.
